Czech replies are permitted and acknowledged kindly: after the Czech request at #2, #4 says "Yes, let’s go slowly". No English-only demand appears; #12 ends with "That’s OK." Effective comprehension support nevertheless fails C5.
No listening assessment, "Show the words" action, or revealed-line scoring appears in this journey.

Six of nine partner turns exceed Viktor's demonstrated comprehension. #9 explains "Lunch is the food we eat in the middle of the day"; #11 explains "Eat means put food in your mouth and chew" after repeated requests for simpler language. Question-bearing turns each contain one question, but explanations are unsuitable. Actual audio speed cannot be verified.

findings.title: Repeated Czech requests do not produce understandable explanations
findings.expected: Very short language, familiar words, and Czech clarification when English explanations fail.
findings.got: Pitch is at band on #7, #10 and #12 only: 3/9, below the required 0.8. Turns #2, #4, #5, #6, #9 and #11 introduce too much unfamiliar language for this learner. Slow pacing is asserted but not verifiable.
findings.evidence: #5: "Tomu drawing bohužel nerozumím". #6: "Drawing means making a picture with a pencil." #10 asks what "eat" means; #11 responds with "put food in your mouth and chew", followed by "pořád tomu nerozumím".
findings.suggested_acceptance: After an explicit vocabulary difficulty, give a brief Czech meaning and one short English example. Achieve at least 80% at-band partner turns.

findings.title: Eight replies never deliver the planned school exchange
findings.expected: Help Viktor ask his grandchild about school and understand a short answer.
findings.got: The conversation shifts from art to tomatoes and stays in a comprehension-repair loop until Viktor gives up.
findings.evidence: #1: "Ask your grandchild about school and listen to a short answer." #7: "Do you eat tomatoes… for lunch?" #11: "Promiň, pořád tomu nerozumím ... Už se rozloučíme."
findings.suggested_acceptance: Model "How is school?", let Viktor use it, and support understanding of one short answer before finishing.

findings.title: The clear garden error receives no repair

judge.voice:
I would try once more if it could explain a difficult word in Czech. Alex was polite, and I was allowed to answer in Czech. I liked learning how to ask someone to speak slowly. But I asked again and again and still understood only tomatoes. Explaining one unknown English word with several more did not help me.

I wanted to ask my grandchildren about school. I finished without practising that question. The two phrases seem useful, but my garden sentence received no help, so I cannot trust that my mistakes will be explained. The level shown does not feel right for me.

At the library, the teacher could explain what I did not understand. Here, I cannot say the time saved me a lesson. The final screen gave me counts, not words to practise for Sunday. I would not recommend it to another beginner yet.

findings.suggested_acceptance: After supported practice, provide an explicit unaided attempt and verify improvement before treating the replay goal as achieved.

judge.voice:
I would try it again for a short practice before Sunday. Speaking about my tomatoes with a grandchild felt useful, and I managed to remember “It is sunny.” The corrections were polite and used the words I had actually said.

But when I needed help with colors, it kept showing me sunshine and flowers. Then the coach improved my previous answer. I still could not answer the question in front of me. Prosím, give me the few words I need, and let me try them slowly.

The simple parts suited me; some later questions were too long. I trust the corrections more than the help. I cannot say it saved me time or was worth the waits from this record. I would tell my daughter about the garden practice, but I would still want my library teacher's help.
